ticket.title: Extract the AST vocabulary miter-polyglot needs, so the grammar table can leave miter
ticket.description:
PREREQUISITE for moving miter-polyglot to common, measured 2026-11-06. miter-polyglot depends on miter-ast and constructs AstIndexer, FunctionSymbol, FunctionNode and Param (miter/crates/polyglot/src/symbol.rs:42-91), so relocating it would put a foundation crate on top of a miter domain crate - an upward edge, which the layer model forbids. It also means every dado and joiner build transitively carries miter-ast and its tree-sitter grammar table today.

Scope: identify exactly which miter-ast items polyglot consumes (symbol.rs: Param, FunctionSymbol, FunctionNode, AstIndexer::encode, seed_from_text, signature_of), decide whether they are AST-indexer wiring or a shared code-model vocabulary, and if the latter extract them into a foundation crate under common. miter-ast then re-exports them so its own paths keep resolving, exactly as miter does for gaugeblock-security.

Do not start until the owner calls it: test 2 of the four admission tests (a measured reduction) is unproven here, and GB-160 says a hunch about weight is not a measurement.
acceptance_criteria:
DONE 2026-11-06. Commit 9b79643 (common) + d2f8573 (dado). The last lateral edge in the graph is gone and the allowlist is now empty.

The edge: dado-core depended on miter-polyglot to answer "does this generated code parse?". That made a code generator reach sideways into a code indexer for a property of neither product.

The extraction was smaller than the ticket assumed, and the reason is worth recording: the vocabulary already existed. gaugeblock-contracts has carried the full Language enum since GB-143, so the new gaugeblock-syntax crate adds the reading of that vocabulary - grammar_for, parser_for, and the syntax diagnostics - rather than a third language enum. A second enum would have been a second table that can disagree with the first, the exact failure GB-148 recorded when dado kept its own parser copy and drifted.

What stayed put: the per-grammar node-kind specs (GrammarSpec, spec_for) are about indexing declarations rather than parsing, so they remain in miter-ast beside the walker that needs them. The grammar *handle* table left miter; the declaration-shape table did not.

The dado side shrank rather than moved: it never needed polyglot's format taxonomy (SQL, HTML, CSS, Markdown, Docker, HCL, Kubernetes), only the five grammar-backed languages, so polyglot_language() and its index_language() indirection are deleted and the wire Language passes straight through. miter-polyglot is gone from the manifest, not merely unused. Declarative formats are still rejected as Unsupported rather than silently accepted.

Graph state: lateral edges 1 -> 0, allowlist empty, downward 154 -> 155, upward 0, verdict clean. That is GB-204's stated goal - burn the lateral edges and empty the allowlist - reached from 19 entries.

Gates: common 111 tests and dado 14 tests green, both clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; docs 108 present 0 drifted after adding the boundary-type spec and both architecture inventories; 11/11 lockfiles fresh, including benchwork and joiner whose locks moved transitively; audit clean.

verification_receipt.command: miter contracts && outfeed lockfiles && miter audit --path . --threshold 250 && chalkline docs check --workspace
